summary: Intro call to surface Holloway Finance's security bar and deployment preferences across Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Main concerns: encryption/KMS integration, SSO/SAML and RBAC, audit log retention and tamper evidence, SOC2/ISO evidence, and multi-region data residency. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share compliance artifacts and propose Dedicated benchmark windows; customer to provide data classification and list of stakeholders for a technical deep dive.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
questions: Can Redwood integrate with our on-prem KMS/HSM?
What audit log retention and export options exist?
Does Dedicated provide physical isolation or just reserved capacity?
How does RBAC map to our SSO groups?
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-07
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (AE), Liam Ortiz (SE), Sofia Park (CSM) - Redwood; Daniel Holloway (CTO), Priya Nair (Head of Security), Carlos Vega (Lead DevOps), Ana Mendes (Compliance) - Holloway Finance

Summary (auto): high-level security/discovery around hosted vs dedicated vs private options, KMS, SSO, audit logs, and compliance evidence.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, can you hear me ok?
[00:03] Daniel Holloway: loud and clear, thanks Maya. we wanted to do a quick intake to understand the security posture and options, we have some regulatory constraints so wanted to map those out.
[00:12] Priya Nair: yes hi all, im priya, head of security at holloway, our main asks are around auditability, encryption, and how we can ensure data residency.
[00:20] Maya Chen: great, yes high level we'll cover SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO flow, RBAC mapping, audit logs and KMS options across hosted, dedicated, private — and then surface what a pilot could look like.
[00:30] Carlos Vega: quick note, we're running a mixed cloud/colocated setup right now, some services on aws, some on-prem. so the ability to use our KMS is a must ideally.
[00:36] Liam Ortiz: (SE) yeah and just to add, when we say customer-managed KMS we mean customer keys used for encryption at rest; some customers bring KMS from cloud providers or HSM, others need an on-prem HSM via network link. latency and egress are considerations.
[00:47] Ana Mendes: we also need to understand retention windows — for audit logs specifically — and how long Redwood keeps transcriptions and prompts. some records are retention 7 years for us.
[00:55] Maya Chen: totally understood. quick qual: are you leaning toward hosted for speed or are you already targeting Dedicated/Private because of compliance?
[01:02] Daniel Holloway: We're open, but the procurement team prefers the predictability of Dedicated if it meets the compliance requirements. Hosted would be fine for non-PII workloads.
[01:12] Priya Nair: but we need to be sure audit trails are tamper-evident and we can export logs into our SIEM, also SSO must be enforced via SAML and group mapping for RBAC.
[01:22] Sofia Park: (CSM) we can absolutely export audit logs to your Splunk/Datadog/ELK, and we have options for immutable storage snapshots for tamper evidence. i'll capture details to follow up.
[01:31] Liam Ortiz: on the RBAC side we map IdP groups to Redwood roles; we support SAML 2.0 and OIDC, single sign-on from Okta, Azure AD, and generic SAML providers. mapping can be auto-provisioned or manual depending on your IdP schema.
[01:43] Carlos Vega: ok, what about SEA — i mean SSO flows? sometimes SAML assertion attributes are inconsistent and provisioning breaks. thoughts?
[01:49] Maya Chen: yep, that happens. we normally validate attributes in a test IdP integration and provide a sample attribute map. if you have custom claim names we can configure custom mappings.
[01:58] Daniel Holloway: how about encryption keys — can we bring our own keys and have them never leave our control?
[02:03] Liam Ortiz: yes, for Private deployments you always retain keys. For Dedicated we offer a BYOK flow where keys are in your cloud KMS (e.g., AWS KMS) and Redwood instances can use short-lived grants; for hosted we also support BYOK via external KMS, but there are nuances on network egress and envelope encryption.
[02:18] Priya Nair: what's the attestation for SOC 2? do you have Type II reports and can we get scoping details?
[02:24] Maya Chen: we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 artifacts. i'll share redacted reports and the control mapping to common frameworks. note that hosted and dedicated share many controls but Private adds additional physical/network isolation controls.
[02:36] Ana Mendes: will the SOC 2 report list services and boundaries? we need to check the service boundary for multi-tenant hosted.
[02:42] Maya Chen: yes, the report has a control matrix and scoping. for hosted we document the multi-tenant controls; for Dedicated we include tenancy segregation details.
[02:49] Daniel Holloway: on retention, you mentioned transcripts and prompts — do you store raw prompts by default?
[02:54] Sofia Park: by default we have configurable retention windows; customers can request zero-retention for prompts in Private and Dedicated. Hosted has optional retention settings and audit logging. we'll follow up with exact TTL values.
[03:05] Carlos Vega: do you support encryption of logs at rest and in transit? we have strict requirements for TLS 1.2+ and AES-256 at rest.
[03:12] Liam Ortiz: yes, TLS 1.2/1.3 in transit and AES-256 for data at rest. the algorithm used is documented in our security page. if you need FIPS validated modules or HSM-backed keys that's part of the Private offering.
[03:23] Priya Nair: how are audit logs protected from tampering? is there WORM or append-only?
[03:28] Maya Chen: we have append-only log storage and can forward to your SIEM in near-real time; for tamper-evidence we can provide signed digests and support immutable S3 buckets or equivalent.
[03:37] Ana Mendes: and when logs are exported to our SIEM, do they include request/response content or just metadata? we need to control PII flow.
[03:44] Liam Ortiz: we can configure what fields are exported. for PII you can mask or redact before export; we also support forwarding metadata-only streams.
[03:52] Daniel Holloway: great. another one: we use a vendor called X for model evaluations, and their team worried about tokenization/PII leakage in model outputs — any mitigations?
[04:01] Maya Chen: Redwood has built-in content filtering and prompt redaction toggles; for higher assurance customers prefer to run a dedicated model variant with stricter filters and local caching to minimize exposure.
[04:12] Priya Nair: question on identity: can Redwood enforce MFA for all users and block service tokens to particular roles?
[04:18] Sofia Park: yes, enforced MFA via IdP is supported. service tokens are scoped; you can provision route-level tokens and restrict by model/route, and rotate tokens programmatically.
[04:26] Carlos Vega: curious about network topology for Dedicated — is it single-tenant VPC peering or shared VPC with isolation?
[04:33] Liam Ortiz: Dedicated commonly deploys into a dedicated account/VPC per customer with peering or private link to customer networks; we can also provide host isolation. the exact pattern depends on cloud partner.
[04:44] Daniel Holloway: and on cost — Dedicated means reserved capacity pricing but also predictable latency, right?
[04:49] Maya Chen: correct; Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput SLAs. Hosted is variable but cheaper for bursty non-sensitive workloads. Private is more expensive but gives full control.
[04:59] Priya Nair: in terms of certs, is Redwood ISO 27001 certified? we had a vendor check asking that specifically.
[05:05] Maya Chen: yes we have ISO 27001 certification. i'll include summary and scope details in the follow-up.
[05:12] Ana Mendes: for the pilot, we'll need a list of stakeholders — security, infra, legal — and a proposed timeline.
[05:18] Maya Chen: perfect, could you share stakeholders by next week? we'll draft a pilot plan with two Dedicated benchmark windows, each 2 hours, and a Private option exploratory timeline.
[05:27] Daniel Holloway: yes we'll compile and email that.
[05:30] Priya Nair: few technical nitpicks: how does KV cache behave in Dedicated/Private? we worry about cached prompt leakage across tenants.
[05:38] Liam Ortiz: KV caches are per-instance and per-model; in Dedicated/Private we guarantee cache isolation. in hosted shared runtime caches are logically isolated but we can enable stronger isolation for sensitive routes.
[05:49] Carlos Vega: ok. any considerations for data residency in eu? we have eudata that can't leave eu.
[05:55] Maya Chen: we have region-specific deployments and routing policies; for EU-only data we can pin to eu-region hosts and enforce no-cross-region fallback. that would be in Dedicated or Private to ensure strict routing.
[06:06] Ana Mendes: final question: can we get a short architecture diagram and a checklist for procurement? legal will need indemnity and data processing addendum.
[06:14] Sofia Park: yes we'll send an architecture deck and a procurement checklist including DPA template and scoping for indemnities.
[06:20] Maya Chen: ok to recap real quick — action items: we'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts, propose Dedicated benchmark windows, send an architecture deck and DPA; you will share stakeholders, data classification, and retention table. sound right?
[06:33] Daniel Holloway: yep that's correct.
[06:36] Priya Nair: thank you, this was helpful.
[06:38] Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with docs and a proposed schedule.
[06:42] Meeting end.
notes: Call included AE+SE and CSM. Customer emphasized KMS BYOK, SSO/SAML mapping, audit log tamper evidence, and data residency. Agreed pilot and artifact exchange. Some transcription artifacts: 'SEA' for SSO, 'KV cache' occasionally spelled 'K V cache'.
